title: Selective Isolation of Lipid Classes from Cold-Water Corals via SPE for Quantitative Fatty Acid Profiling
author: Audrey M. Pruski
materials: Flash-freeze Sample on board to prevent degradation
Condition a third cartridge (C3) as above
Stack C2 onto C3 using an adapter

Preparation of Working Solutions - Transmethylation reagent: 3.4 mL Methanol + 0.6 mL H₂SO₄ (98%), and 4.0 mL CHCl₃ with BHT (50 mg/L). Keep at 4 °C in a flammable storage refrigerator Reagent should be cold and freshly prepared - C19:0 (internal standard) stock solution ~1 mg.mL ‑1 in hexane. The solution is diluted before use (1/9). Keep at -20 °C Adjust the concentration of the internal standard so that its peak on the chromatogram falls within the range of peak intensities, ideally between the most abundant and the least abundant fatty acids. This ensures accurate quantification across the entire dynamic range

steps.title: Sample Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the coral samples for extraction.

substeps.instruction: Freeze-dry samples and store at -80 °C until analysis.
Grind freeze-dried sample into a fine powder using a bead mill homogenizer, keeping the chamber filled with liquid nitrogen to prevent heating.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare and store the following reagents at 4 °C in a refrigerator (flammable storage where applicable):

substeps.instruction: Chloroform/methanol/water (1:2:0.8) reagent: 5.265 mL CHCl₃, 10.525 mL CH₃OH, and 4.21 mL H₂O.
1M NaCl solution in ultrapure water (58g.L⁻¹).
0.3N NaOH solution (12 g.L⁻¹).
0.2M H₃PO₄ solution (19.6g.L⁻¹).
BHT (butylated hydroxytoluene) at 50 mg.mL⁻¹ in Chloroform.

steps.title: Total Lipid Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract total lipids using a modified Bligh and Dyer method.

substeps.instruction: Place ~3 g of freeze-dried sample in a 30 mL glass tube (round bottom, screw tap with PTFE liner).
Add 20 mL of CHCl₃/CH₃OH/H₂O (1:2:0.8) containing 1M NaCl and 0.2M H₃PO₄.
Sonicate for 5 minutes (on ice if needed), then rotate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Add 2.5 mL CHCl₃, then 2.5 mL H₂O; shake for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 2500 rpm, 4 °C, for 5 minutes and recover the bottom organic phase using a Pasteur pipette.
Repeat the extraction 3 times with 5 mL CHCl₃.
Pool all organic phases (final volume ≈ 22.765 mL) and vortex, keeping the phase cold on ice.

steps.title: Organic Phase Washing and Concentration
steps.instruction: Purify and concentrate the extracted lipids.

substeps.instruction: Wash the organic phase with 2.5 mL cold 0.3N NaOH; shake for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 2500 rpm, 4 °C, for 5 minutes and recover the organic phase.

Transfer 20 mL or more of the organic phase into a new glass tube (conical bottom, screw tap with PTFE liner) and evaporate at 40 °C under vacuum using a rotary evaporator (do not allow lipids to dry out).
Cool at -20 °C and redissolve in 400 µL CHCl₃ + BHT (50 mg.L⁻¹).
Centrifuge at 2000 rpm, 4 °C, for 5 minutes and store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Primary Lipid Separation (C1 Cartridge)
steps.instruction: Separate neutral lipids, fatty acids, and phospholipids using a Strata NH₂ (aminopropyl silica) cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Condition the first cartridge (C1) with 2 × 2 mL hexane and vacuum dry for 2–5 min.
Load 390 µL lipid extract and vacuum to dryness.
Elute neutral lipids (E1) using 4 × 2 mL of Solvent A (Chloroform:2-propanol 2:1 v/v).
Elute free fatty acids (E2) using 4 × 2 mL of Solvent B (2% Acetic acid in diethyl ether).
Elute phospholipids (E3) using 4 × 2 mL of Solvent C (Methanol).
Store eluates at -20 °C.

steps.title: Neutral Lipid Fractionation (C2 Cartridge)
steps.instruction: Further fractionate the neutral lipid extract (E1).

substeps.instruction: Condition a second cartridge (C2) with hexane as described for C1.
Load 390 µL from E1 (do not dry).
Elute wax esters and sterol esters (E4) using 4 × 2 mL of Solvent D (Hexane).
Elute triglycerides (E5) using 6 × 2 mL of Solvent E (1% Diethyl ether + 10% Dichloromethane in hexane).
Elute sterols (E6) using 9 × 2 mL of Solvent F (5% Ethyl acetate in hexane).
Remove C3 (if present), place C2 back on manifold, and elute diglycerides (E7) using 4 × 2 mL of Solvent G (15% Ethyl acetate in hexane).
Elute monoglycerides (E8) using 4 × 2 mL of Solvent H (Chloroform:Methanol 2:1 v/v).

steps.title: Eluate Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Process the fractionated eluates for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Evaporate all eluates under vacuum at 45 °C.
Redissolve in 100 µL CHCl₃ + BHT and store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Transmethylation of Fatty Acids
steps.instruction: Convert lipids to fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs) for GC-MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: To eluates E2, E3, E4, E5, E7, and E8: add 20 µL internal standard C19:0 and 8 mL of transmethylation reagent; cap and shake.
Incubate for 1 hour 30 minutes at 90 °C, shaking occasionally (3-4 times).
Cool on ice or at -20 °C and open carefully.
Recover the lower organic phase in a new glass tube.
Add 2 mL cold H₂O, vortex, and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 3000 rpm, 4 °C.

steps.title: FAME Purification and Final Preparation
steps.instruction: Clean and prepare the FAME extracts for GC-MS.

substeps.instruction: Discard the upper polar layer and transfer 6-9 mL of the lower organic phase to a clean screw-cap tube.
Wash with 4 mL cold 2% K₂CO₃; centrifuge at 3000 rpm, 4 °C, for 5 minutes.
Re-extract the aqueous phase 2 times with 2 mL cold hexane:CHCl₃ (4:1).
Transfer to GC vials with a 200 µl insert and store at -80 °C.
Redissolve in 30-50 µL pure hexane and vortex at 3000 rpm, 4 °C, for 5 minutes.
Evaporate solvent in a SpeedVac concentrator at room temperature and cool at -20 °C.
